intent: Hold the search text and the highlighted item of one searchable, keyboard-navigable list of commands, and filter and rank its items by what the user types.
typical_uses: A list of actions the user narrows down by typing and runs with Enter or a click
A searchable list embedded in a page or a panel, rather than in an overlay

dont_use_when.situation: The searchable list should open as an overlay above the page, such as from a keyboard shortcut
A value picked from a searchable list and kept as the field's value
A short menu of actions anchored to a trigger button, with no need to search
One value from a short fixed list with no need to search

invariants.text: `value` is the value of the highlighted item, not a chosen one: `defaultValue` seeds the initial highlight and is ignored afterwards, every change of a given `value` moves the highlight to the item with that value, and only while `value` is given does a keyboard or pointer move report the newly highlighted item's value through `onValueChange`. Running an item is reported by that item's own `onSelect`.

While the search text is not empty, each item is scored against it (by `filter` when given, otherwise the library's built-in fuzzy score, over the item's value and `keywords`); items scoring 0 are not rendered, the rest are sorted by score, and a group with no remaining item is hidden. `shouldFilter={false}` turns scoring and sorting off and leaves rendering the matching items to the caller.

The root handles keys pressed anywhere inside it: ArrowDown and ArrowUp move the highlight (wrapping only with `loop`), Home and End jump to the first and last item, Enter runs the highlighted item, and Ctrl+N/J and Ctrl+P/K move down and up unless `vimBindings` is false. Disabled items are skipped.

`label` is rendered as a visually hidden `<label>` for the search input, and the input's `aria-labelledby` always points at it; an `aria-label` on the root names only the root div, which carries no role.

anti_patterns.dont: Name the palette with `aria-label` on the root and leave `label` out
anti_patterns.do_instead: Pass `label`; it is the text the search input is labelled by

anti_patterns.dont: Filter the items by hand while the root still filters them
anti_patterns.do_instead: Either let the root filter (the default), or pass `shouldFilter={false}` and render only the items that match

children.states: children is the root's content, React nodes holding CommandInput and CommandList
children.because: `React.ReactNode` is a union of elements, strings, numbers, fragments and more; the compiler emits one JSON type per property.

defaultValue.states: defaultValue is the value of the item highlighted when the root first renders
defaultValue.because: The library types it as `string`, but the root's props also inherit the div's own `defaultValue` attribute, and the intersection prints as `string | (readonly string[] & string)` - the compiler emits one JSON type per property. Pass a string.

filter.states: filter is a function scoring an item against the search text, from 0 (hidden) to 1 (best match)
filter.because: `(value: string, search: string, keywords?: string[]) => number` - a function, which no JSON Schema type covers. Without it the library's built-in fuzzy score is used.

onValueChange.states: onValueChange is a callback called with the newly highlighted item's value, not a value
onValueChange.because: `(value: string) => void` - a function, which no JSON Schema type covers. It is called only while `value` is given (see value-is-the-highlighted-item).

unexposed_parts.reason: The root renders a visually hidden `<label>` holding `label` before its children; it is fixed markup of the root, not a component of its own.

good.title: A searchable list of actions with groups
good.code:
<Command label="Commands">
  <CommandInput placeholder="Type a command or search..." />
  <CommandList>
    <CommandEmpty>No results found.</CommandEmpty>
    <CommandGroup heading="Suggestions">
      <CommandItem value="calendar" onSelect={openCalendar}>Calendar</CommandItem>
      <CommandItem value="calculator" onSelect={openCalculator}>Calculator</CommandItem>
    </CommandGroup>
  </CommandList>
</Command>

good.title: Filtering done by the caller
good.code:
<Command label="Files" shouldFilter={false}>
  <CommandInput value={query} onValueChange={setQuery} />
  <CommandList>
    {results.map((file) => (
      <CommandItem key={file.id} value={file.id} onSelect={() => open(file)}>
        {file.name}
      </CommandItem>
    ))}
  </CommandList>
</Command>

bad.title: Items placed straight under the root
bad.why: Items belong inside CommandList, which renders the listbox the input points at through `aria-controls`; items outside it are options with no listbox, and the list's height and scrolling do not apply; the root looks for items only inside the list, so arrow keys and Enter never reach them.
